title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 35 (Civil Liability for Mis-statements in Prospectus)

content.overview: Section 35 creates civil compensation liability where a person has subscribed for securities of a company acting on any statement included, or the inclusion or omission of any matter, in the prospectus which is misleading and has sustained loss or damage as a consequence. Specified persons including the company, directors, promoters and persons who authorised the issue are liable, subject to statutory defences. Where the prospectus was issued with intent to defraud or for a fraudulent purpose, every person referred to in the section is personally responsible without limitation of liability.
content.glance: Reliance on misleading prospectus statement/inclusion/omission; loss; liability of company, directors, promoters, authorisers and certain experts; defences; unlimited liability if fraud proved.
content.study: Where a person has subscribed for securities acting on any statement included, or the inclusion or omission of any matter, in the prospectus which is misleading and has sustained loss or damage as a consequence, the company and every person who is a director at the time of issue, named as director or agreed to become director, a promoter, or who has authorised the issue of the prospectus, and every expert who is liable under the section, are liable to pay compensation. Statutory defences include withdrawal of consent before issue, issue without knowledge or consent, and reasonable belief in truth. Where it is proved that a prospectus was issued with intent to defraud or for any fraudulent purpose, every person referred to in the section is personally responsible without any limitation of liability. Current-law framing: prove subscription on a misleading prospectus matter, loss, and the class of defendant; then test defences and any fraud allegation.

sections.heading: Cause of Action
sections.body: Subscription acting on a misleading statement, inclusion or omission in the prospectus, causing loss or damage.

sections.heading: Persons Liable
sections.body: Company; directors at time of issue; named/proposed directors; promoters; persons who authorised issue; experts as specified.

sections.heading: Defences
sections.body: Statutory defences include withdrawal of consent, issue without knowledge/consent, and reasonable belief in truth of the statement.

sections.heading: Fraudulent Prospectus
sections.body: If the prospectus was issued with intent to defraud or for a fraudulent purpose, liability is personal and unlimited for the persons referred to in the section.

provisions.title: Civil liability for mis-statements in prospectus

examples.title: Investor loss on misleading prospectus
examples.body: An investor subscribes on the basis of a misleading profit forecast in the prospectus and suffers loss. Section 35 supports a compensation claim against the statutory classes of defendants, subject to defences.

examples.title: Director who withdrew consent
examples.body: A proposed director withdrew consent before issue and the prospectus was issued without that person’s authority. A statutory defence may apply.

hypotheticals.question: Must the claimant prove fraud for ordinary s. 35 compensation?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Ordinary s. 35 liability is for loss from reliance on a misleading prospectus matter; fraud escalates to unlimited personal liability.

distinctions.title: Civil liability (s. 35) vs criminal liability (s. 34)
distinctions.right: Criminal liability of authorisers under s. 447

misconceptions.trap: Only the company can be sued for prospectus misstatements.
misconceptions.correction: Section 35 lists the company, directors, promoters, authorisers and certain experts as potentially liable.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 35 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Prove subscription on misleading prospectus matter and loss. II. Identify defendant class. III. Test defences. IV. Address fraud/unlimited liability if alleged. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Reliance; loss; defendant class; defences; fraud allegation if any; precise relief.

examTips: Structure: reliance + loss + defendant class + defences.
Separate ordinary compensation from fraudulent unlimited liability.
